item.vignette: A 6-year-old boy has severe intellectual disability, absent speech, seizures beginning in infancy, truncal ataxia, and progressive postnatal microcephaly. Genetic testing identifies a hemizygous loss-of-function variant in SLC9A6.
item.lead_in: The affected protein normally performs which cellular function?

options.A: Methyl-CpG-dependent regulation of neuronal gene transcription
options.B: Ubiquitination of neuronal proteins by the maternally expressed UBE3A allele
options.C: Transport of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes
options.D: Formation of connexin-32 channels in peripheral myelin
options.E: Electroneutral sodium-hydrogen exchange that helps regulate endosomal pH

item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; genotype is provided and the item tests the specific endosomal transport function of NHE6.
item.tested_construct: SLC9A6 encodes endosomal NHE6, a Na+/H+ exchanger that regulates intra-endosomal pH

explanation.key_explanation: SLC9A6 encodes NHE6, an endosomal sodium-hydrogen exchanger. NHE6 exchanges sodium for protons and helps regulate intra-endosomal pH; loss-of-function causes Christianson syndrome.

distractor_explanations.A: MECP2 participates in methyl-CpG-dependent gene regulation and is linked to Rett syndrome.
distractor_explanations.B: Loss of maternal UBE3A function causes Angelman syndrome.
distractor_explanations.C: ABCD1 mediates peroxisomal very-long-chain fatty-acid transport.
distractor_explanations.D: GJB1 encodes connexin 32 in peripheral myelin.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. NHE6 is an endosomal Na+/H+ exchanger involved in control of endosomal pH.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize SLC9A6/NHE6 as an endosomal sodium-hydrogen exchanger required for normal endosomal pH regulation in Christianson syndrome.

evidence_map.claim: SLC9A6 encodes NHE6, an endosomal Na+/H+ exchanger that mediates sodium-proton exchange and regulates intra-endosomal pH.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains the cellular defect in a boy with Christianson syndrome.
